title: Non-coding Regulatory Variants in ASD (Autism Spectrum Disorders) Disrupt CTCF Domains and Shape Cell-Type-Specific Neurodevelopmental Landscapes Revealed by Single-Cell Analyses and Cortical Organoids.
abstract: Targeted sequencing of 85,394 active cCREs (ENCODE v2) in 600 samples (200 trios) negative for pathogenic coding variants. Sei-predicted regulatory impact scores for de novo and ultra-rare inherited variants; target genes mapped with T-Gene. 164 de novo variants in 103 probands and 53,023 ultra-rare inherited variants. De novo variants enriched in promoter-like sequences (p=0.02), 53.19% affecting CTCF boundaries; inherited variants enriched for CTCF-binding loss (p=1.55e-8) with maternal transmission bias. snRNA-seq (ASD/control brains) and Cortical Organoid Atlas profiling showed de novo target genes (POGZ, ROCK2, NFIB) with dynamic, cell-type- and stage-specific expression vs constitutive expression of inherited target genes (SYNJ2, UBC, CLU, DLC1). De novo regulatory target genes overlap known ASD coding-risk genes (POGZ, NFIB).
methods: Targeted sequencing of 85,394 ENCODE cCREs in 200 trios; Sei regulatory-impact prediction; T-Gene target mapping; snRNA-seq (64 brains) and Cortical Organoid Atlas scRNA-seq.
summary: Targeted sequencing of 85,394 regulatory elements in 200 coding-negative ASD trios. De novo regulatory variants concentrate in promoters and CTCF boundaries and map to dynamically expressed genes (POGZ, NFIB, ROCK2) that overlap known ASD coding-risk genes; inherited variants hit CTCF-binding sites and constitutively expressed genes. Directly on-target for the atlas: a coding-negative cohort, regulatory-variant focus, and cell-type/stage-resolved expression. Association-level, preprint, not independently validated.
